title: Quality Gates and Continuous Integration
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of Quality Gates and Continuous Integration in a Vue 3 application.
Apply at least one of the syllabus subtopics in a small, inspectable example.
Verify one expected behavior and identify a relevant edge case.

content.intro: This lesson studies Quality Gates and Continuous Integration within Testing and Quality Assurance. The source PDF subtopics are preserved below and connected to an original working-style example.
content.why_it_matters: Testing behavior before release catches regressions in props, events, forms, asynchronous states, and routing.

content_blocks.title: Quality Gates and Continuous Integration: Behavior-focused testing
content_blocks.alt_text: Behavior-focused testing diagram for lesson 123: Quality Gates and Continuous Integration. Create known state and deterministic inputs → Trigger the user behavior or failure case → Check visible output, events, and errors
content_blocks.caption: Testing workflow: arrange a repeatable state, act as a user, then assert observable behavior including a boundary case.

content_blocks.title: The idea in context
content_blocks.text: Automated checks combine unit, component, interaction, integration, and end-to-end tests with repeatable quality gates. This lesson focuses on Quality Gates and Continuous Integration. Start by naming the state, component, browser behavior, or deployment boundary involved; then predict what should change and test the smallest example.

items.title: Running tests automatically
items.text: For Running tests automatically, define the behavior a user can observe before writing the assertion. Test a typical case and one boundary/failure case, keep dependencies deterministic, and use component or browser tests only when that level adds confidence.

items.title: Linting and formatting checks
items.text: For Linting and formatting checks, bind the input to a clear state value, validate before submission, and associate field errors with their controls. A disabled or loading state should be reflected in the UI without treating the client as the authority for server validation.

items.title: Type checks where applicable
items.text: For Type checks where applicable, TypeScript is a recommended specialization rather than a prerequisite for the JavaScript path. Use types to make component contracts and external data assumptions explicit, and keep runtime validation for values received from an API.

items.title: Test coverage reports
items.text: For Test coverage reports, define the behavior a user can observe before writing the assertion. Test a typical case and one boundary/failure case, keep dependencies deterministic, and use component or browser tests only when that level adds confidence.

items.title: Preventing regressions before deployment
items.text: For Preventing regressions before deployment, document what data enters the component, which events leave it, and where shared content or behavior belongs. Keep props one-way, emit changes rather than mutating parent-owned values, and add slots only when a real composition point is needed.

content_blocks.expected_output: The assertion verifies a stable portion of the localized currency output; exact symbols and spacing can vary by runtime/locale data.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Place in a JavaScript test file in a Vue project with Vitest configured. Test a pure utility separately from a component test.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the initial values or original code, reload the development app/test, and repeat once with a boundary or failure case. Remove temporary logs and test data before committing.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Work through Quality Gates and Continuous Integration with a predict–change–verify loop. First state the expected UI or console output. Change only the relevant input/state value, then observe the result. Compare it with the expected output in the code block; if it differs, check the exact file, runtime/version, browser Console, and network response before widening the investigation.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Extend the example to include “Linting and formatting checks”. Keep the same behavior for the ordinary input, then try an empty, invalid, repeated, or failure condition that makes sense for the example. Record the expected result before testing.

items.title: Assuming behavior instead of checking it
items.text: Write down the expected result and reproduce the issue in the smallest possible example; inspect the browser Console and the exact reactive value or request.

items.title: Ignoring an edge case
items.text: Try empty input, a missing item, repeated interaction, a failed request, or unmounting while work is pending; handle the case explicitly.

items.title: Putting every responsibility in one component
items.text: Separate display, reusable logic, API service, and shared state when that boundary makes the behavior easier to test and explain.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: Remember: Automated checks combine unit, component, interaction, integration, and end-to-end tests with repeatable quality gates. For Quality Gates and Continuous Integration, keep the example small, verify the rendered or logged result, and consult the official references when behavior depends on a specific Vue or ecosystem version.

content_blocks.title: Accessibility, version, and runtime notes
content_blocks.text: Use semantic HTML, readable labels, keyboard-operable controls, and visible errors where the example interacts with users. Vue examples are intended for Vue 3.x with create-vue/Vite unless a legacy or specialist lesson explicitly says otherwise. This CodeLeaf playground does not execute arbitrary Vue code; the snippets are labeled for static validation and should be run in a separate local project.

content.task: Create a small example for “Quality Gates and Continuous Integration” that applies “Running tests automatically”, predicts the expected result, and verifies a relevant boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates the named Vue concept rather than only mentioning it.
The expected output or observable behavior is written down and can be checked locally.
At least one boundary, loading, invalid-input, or failure case is tested or explicitly reasoned about.
The example uses semantic/accessible interaction patterns and does not treat frontend state as authoritative security.
hints: Start with the smallest observable part of “Running tests automatically”.
Predict the output before changing one input at a time.
Use the browser Console, Vue DevTools, or the appropriate test runner to isolate a mismatch.

common_mistakes.problem: The example only covers the happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Real interfaces receive empty values, delayed responses, invalid input, and failed requests.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one realistic edge/failure case and state its expected behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: The code assumes an API or feature exists in every runtime.
common_mistakes.why: Tool and API support depends on Vue, the build tool, or the chosen SSR/test framework.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the linked official reference and record the runtime/version assumption.

summary: Quality Gates and Continuous Integration belongs to the broader area Testing and Quality Assurance.
The main concept to practice is Running tests automatically.
Verify a normal result and one meaningful boundary case before using the pattern in a production feature.
